note: Live parity checks that are known Rust-versus-Python divergences. Each path is a leaf and pins the Python and Rust values. Round-trip entries use the same rules. A pattern that names a list or object is rejected, and a [*] wildcard is rejected. Any other difference, or any other value at a listed path, fails the job. A listed path that stops differing fails the job, so this list stays exact. CI prints the list. Contract-board board_effects is wired through Session refresh and the oracle, so broker_board.txt is not listed. Narrative text that no script or golden reaches is not compared, so it is not listed here. One such difference is known: the vendored Python first-contract beat reads "Deliver on time, and doors open. Fail, and they close." and Rust reads "Arrive on time, and doors open. Fail, and they close." (crates/portlight-sim/src/narrative.rs). It appears in no golden, so no golden value depends on it.

entries.summary: A successful prize capture agrees on fleet, crew, and cargo. The capture log row does not. Rust clear_encounter runs before blank_step, so that row's enemy id, name, strength, boarding progress, boarding_threshold (2 vs 0), and enemy crew (5 vs 0) are empty. The oracle builds the row from the encounter first. The golden file is that Python snapshot; these paths, at these values, are the only ones allowed to differ from Rust.

Hunt-fight crew loss is a deliberate Mike-authorized divergence. On an active unclaimed bounty, Rust drops the enemy rake's crew result (roll still drawn, hull kept) and re-reads the boarding player roll as min(cap, floor(0.15+0.025*crew+u), r) with sail-minimum floor. A privateer cutter starts at crew_min 5, so these scripts keep crew 5 (sail hires to 9) where Python keeps 1 (sail hires to 5).
